title: Swift data show no third flare of AT2018fyk in the 2025 windows that the repeating partial disruption model predicted; a copy of the 2022 flare that starts before December 2025 is below 5% in UV
abstract: AT2018fyk is a tidal disruption event that stopped, came back, and stopped again in August 2023. Wevers et al. (2023) and Pasham et al. (2024) explained this with a repeating partial tidal disruption and predicted a third rise in March 2025 or in 15 May to 31 August 2025 (MJD 60864 +- 54). We reduced all 229 public Swift XRT and UVOT observations from 2018 to 2026 with one uniform Python method and tested these predictions. No XRT visit after the 2023 shutoff gives a 3-sigma detection. Stacked 3-sigma limits are 2.7e41 erg/s in early 2025 and 5.4e41 erg/s in the Pasham window, 3 to 6 percent of the 2022 flare peak (8.5e42 erg/s). The UVW1, UVW2 and UVM2 rates in 2025 agree with the 2024 level; in the Pasham window the UVW2 excess is 0.6 +- 0.7 percent of the 2022 peak excess. When we shift the observed 2022-2023 light curve in time and fit its amplitude, the 95 percent upper limit is 1.3-5 percent (UV) for any start date from October 2024 to late November 2025, which includes both predicted windows. XMM-Newton pipeline values from May 2024 also show a low state. Thus the predicted third flare did not occur on time, or it was more than 20 times weaker than the 2022 flare in the UV. The result does not reject all repeating-disruption models: the star can have lost almost no mass, or the fallback time can have changed. Swift made only one 85-s visit after 6 December 2025, so a flare that starts in 2026 is not tested. The luminosity values use one count-rate factor from the soft state.

display.caption: Swift light curve of AT2018fyk, 2018-2026. Top: XRT 0.3-10 keV luminosity (one count-rate factor); blue points are 3-sigma detections, grey triangles one-visit 3-sigma limits, black bars stacked windows. Bottom: UVOT count rates in a 5-arcsec aperture (host included). Violet and orange bands: predicted third-rise windows of Wevers et al. (2023) and Pasham et al. (2024). Dotted lines: the two shutoffs.
Detail for 2023-2026. No XRT visit after the August 2023 shutoff gives a detection. The 2025 window limits are 3-6 percent of the 2022 peak. The UV rates are flat from 2024 to December 2025.

95 percent upper limit on the amplitude of a time-shifted copy of the observed 2022-2023 flare, as a function of its start date (1 = same as the 2022 flare). Blue: X-ray Poisson fit. Orange: UV excess above the 2024 level. Starts after the last 2025 visit (6 December 2025) are poorly constrained.

citations.reason: Wevers et al. 2023 predicted the third rebrightening near day 2400 (March 2025); Swift data show none.
Pasham et al. 2024 predicted a rise at MJD 60864 +- 54; Swift data show none. We use their Swift luminosities to set the count-rate factor.
Published AT2018fyk Swift luminosities (CC BY 4.0) used for the count-rate to luminosity factor and a UVW1 calibration comparison.
